why: The printed final line gives the unit of the rate constant as mol^-1 L^-1 s^-1, which contradicts the substitution printed immediately above it: (mol L^-1 s^-1) / (mol L^-1)^2 = mol^-1 L s^-1. The exponent of L must be +1, not -1. Shipping the printed unit would teach a second order rate constant the wrong dimensions. The value 1.625 is correct.
solution: [Textbook misprint: the book prints the final unit as \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}\ L^{-1}\ s^{-1}}\), which contradicts its own substitution one line above — \((\mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}\ s^{-1}}) / (\mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}})^2\) gives \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}\ L\ s^{-1}}\), with \(L\) to the power \(+1\). The unit has been corrected here so the worked example does not teach the wrong dimensions for a second order rate constant; the value \(1.625\) is as printed and is correct.]

why: The printed working writes the temperature-dependence relation with 2.303 RT in the denominator, where 2.303 R belongs. The T is spurious: the chapter's own Eq. Preserving the formula as printed would ship a worked example whose stated equation contradicts its own next line and is dimensionally wrong.
solution: [Textbook misprint: the book writes the temperature-dependence relation with \(2.303\,RT\) in the denominator, where \(2.303\,R\) belongs — the temperature is already carried by the bracket \((T_2 - T_1)/T_1T_2\). The chapter's own Eq. (6.23) prints \(E_a/(2.303\,R)\), and this example's own substitution divides by \(2.303 \times 8.314\ \mathrm{J\ K^{-1}mol^{-1}}\) with no \(T\), which is what gives its printed \(2.212\). The formula has been corrected here; the printed answer \(1.464 \times 10^{5}\) min is correct.]
